newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Close finish in Madagascar presidential vote.
newsitem.headline: Close finish in Madagascar presidential vote.

text.p: Former military rule Didier Ratsiraka held a slim lead over Albert Zafy on Sunday in Madagascar's presidential election as results were still awaited from 827 of 14,542 polling stations on the Indian Ocean island.

Figures released by the Interior Ministry showed Ratsiraka with 50.4 percent of the votes counted, against Zafy's 49.3 per cent. Ministry sources said final figures would not be available until later this week.
The election was ordered after the National Assembly impeached Zafy, president since 1993, for contravening the constitution and exceeding his powers.
Fewer than half the eligible voters went to the polls on December 29 in the runoff between the two leading candidates, the latest figures showed.
None of the 15 candidates gained the required 50 percent vote in the first-round poll in November.
Zafy, a 69-year-old medical professor, succeeded Ratsiraka, 60, a former Marxist, in 1993 after a wave of political unrest had paralysed the republic for months.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months in voluntary exile in France to contest the election after Zafy's impeachment.
